adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, existing-attendee filtering uses a case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and blacklist matching only lowercases the blacklist values, not `guest`. Since `guests` are not normalized (e.g., lowercased) before comparison or insertion, `Guest@Example.com` will not match an existing `guest@example.com`, leading to duplicate attendee rows and subsequent duplicate calendar/email notifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The attendee.email === user.email check at addGuests.handler.ts:52 can wrongly deny a legitimate attendee whose email casing differs from the stored row

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts` the authorization check treats attendee emails as case-sensitive: `booking.attendees.find((attendee) => attendee.email === user.email)`. If the stored attendee email casing differs from the authenticated `user.email` casing, `isAttendee` becomes false and the request can be incorrectly rejected with `FORBIDDEN`. The diff shows no normalization (e.g., lowercasing) for either side, and similar exact-match comparisons are used elsewhere (e.g., filtering `uniqueGuests`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is built from the requester's (ctx.user) credentials instead of the organizer's, so when anyone other than the organizer adds guests the calendar event is silently never updated with new attendees

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed using an `EventManager` instantiated with the requester (`ctx.user`) and their credentials (`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`), not the booking organizer’s credentials (`booking.userId`). Since the mutation allows non-organizers to add guests (`isAttendee` passes the permission check), the code can attempt to update the organizer’s calendar attendees using credentials that may not have access to the organizer’s connected calendar, leading to the calendar not being updated as intended for those cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email-sending failures are swallowed in addGuests.handler.ts:165-169: the caught err is discarded and the log line omits it, so guests are committed while no one receives notification and the failure is undiagnosable

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the `sendAddGuestsEmails` call is wrapped in `try/catch` and the catch only does `console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails")` without logging `err` or rethrowing. This is diff-verifiable and makes email failures hard to diagnose while the booking attendee changes have already been committed via `prisma.booking.update(...)`. Whether email failure should block the mutation is a product decision, but discarding the error details is a concrete, actionable issue introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side uniqueness/duplicate guard on guests: the server schema lacks the client-side refine and uniqueGuests only filters existing attendees, so a direct tRPC call with duplicate emails (or concurrent requests) inserts duplicate BookingAttendee rows via createMany

Raw guests input is passed to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of the filtered uniqueGuests, causing emails already attending to be misclassified and re-sent the full AttendeeScheduledEmail instead of the 'new guests added' notice

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, guest emails are filtered into `uniqueGuests` (excluding existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only `uniqueGuests` are actually added to the booking via `createMany`. However, the email notification call uses the raw `guests` input: `await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests);`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts), the `newGuests` array is used to decide whether each attendee gets `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail` (`if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) ...`). Passing unfiltered `guests` means an already-existing attendee email included in the input will be treated as a "new guest" and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` again, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: isInvalidEmail is never reset on success or dialog reopen in AddGuestsDialog.tsx, so the red 'Emails must be unique and valid' banner persists over a fresh, valid form after a prior failed attempt

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed validation (`setIsInvalidEmail(true)` in `handleAdd`), but it is not cleared in the success path (`onSuccess` only calls `setIsOpenDialog(false)` and `setMultiEmailValue([""])`). Since the dialog component stays mounted and state persists across open/close, reopening after a prior invalid attempt can still show the red "Emails must be unique and valid" banner despite a fresh form. It is only reset on the Cancel button handler, not on success or on reopen.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team-member notification branch in sendAddGuestsEmails is unreachable because the CalendarEvent built in the handler never sets a team property, so calendarEvent.team is always undefined and team members are never notified

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the CalendarEvent `evt` passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` is constructed without any `team` property (it sets organizer, attendees, uid, location, etc., but no `team`). adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking status check in addGuests.handler.ts: guests can be added to cancelled/rejected bookings, sending 'Guests added' emails and calendar updates for dead events, and the 'Additional guests' menu item in BookingListItem.tsx lacks status gating

The handler also unconditionally calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and attempts to send `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`, so it will perform calendar/email side effects even if the booking is no longer active. adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side cap on the `guests` array in addGuests.schema.ts — `z.array(z.string().email())` lacks `.max()`, and since the permission check allows any attendee to invoke the mutation, a low-privilege account can trigger unbounded email sending (with live meeting credentials), ICS generation, and DB/email worker exhaustion (mass-email / resource-exhaustion abuse)

adjudication.rationale: The server input schema in `addGuests.schema.ts` is `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()`, so the mutation accepts an unbounded number of emails. The handler (`addGuests.handler.ts`) permits any existing attendee (`isAttendee`) to call it, and then performs `attendees.createMany`, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(...)`, and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which can fan out to many emails/ICS generation. This is a verifiable resource-exhaustion / mass-email abuse vector introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `&&` used instead of `||` in the team admin/owner authorization check in addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 — `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is only true if the user is both admin AND owner, locking out plain team admins/owners and returning FORBIDDEN for team bookings in normal usage

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which only evaluates to true if the user is both a team admin and a team owner. Given the variable name and subsequent permission gate (`if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee) throw FORBIDDEN`), this will incorrectly deny access to users who are admin-only or owner-only for team bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` bypass via case/whitespace mismatch — the blacklist is lowercased but guest emails are compared verbatim via `includes(guest)`, so `Evil@Example.com` bypasses an `evil@example.com` entry and entries with leading spaces never match; the case-sensitive `guest === attendee.email` comparison also fails to dedup case-variants of existing attendee emails, creating duplicate attendee records

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the blacklist is normalized to lowercase (`BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.split(...).map(email => email.toLowerCase())`), but incoming `guest` values are compared verbatim via `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`, so case variants (e.g., `Evil@Example.com`) or whitespace-padded emails won’t match and can bypass the blacklist. Similarly, dedup against existing attendees is `guest === attendee.email` (case-sensitive), allowing case-variant duplicates to be created via `attendees.createMany`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema lacks the intra-request uniqueness validation the client enforces — duplicate emails like `["dup@x.com", "dup@x.com"]` pass both the server schema and the handler's `uniqueGuests` filter (which only dedups against existing attendees), hitting `createMany` and either violating the `(bookingId, email)` unique constraint (unhandled Prisma error → 500) or creating duplicate attendee rows and duplicate emails/invites

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler builds the `EventManager` using the caller (`ctx.user`): it calls `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and constructs `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...] })`. However, the booking organizer is `booking.userId` (and `booking.user` is fetched with `credentials: true` but never used). Because the authz permits non-organizers (`isAttendee` or team admin/owner) to call this mutation, a non-organizer can trigger `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` using their own credentials instead of the organizer’s, which can leave the organizer’s calendar event not updated (or update the wrong account).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Attendee rows are persisted (addGuests.handler.ts:92-106) before the `updateCalendarAttendees` calendar call with no transaction — if the calendar update throws, the request errors out while the guests remain added, leaving partial state

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the DB write happens first: prisma.booking.update(...) creates attendee rows (the createMany on attendees) before the external side effect `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);`. That calendar update is not wrapped in a try/catch and there is no transaction spanning both operations, so if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws, the mutation will error while the new attendee rows remain persisted, producing partial state (DB updated, calendar not).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking status or time check in the unscoped `findFirst` (addGuests.handler.ts:26-42) — guests can be added to cancelled or past bookings and receive `AttendeeScheduledEmail` with an ICS hardcoded to `status: "CONFIRMED"` for events that no longer exist

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the booking lookup is only scoped by `id` (`prisma.booking.findFirst({ where: { id: bookingId } ... })`) and there is no validation against `booking.startTime/endTime` (present and used later to build the `CalendarEvent`) or any booking “cancelled”/inactive state before mutating attendees and sending emails. The email path can send a fresh invite-like email to newly added guests (`sendAddGuestsEmails` sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` when `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`), and the ICS generated in the new add-guests templates is hardcoded to `status: "CONFIRMED"`, which would be incorrect if the booking is in the past or otherwise no longer valid.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failures are swallowed — `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` never logs `err` and the handler returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`, so guests may be persisted with nobody notified while the organizer sees a success toast and the failure is undetectable in production

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler still returns success (`return { message: "Guests added" };`). This means email failures are intentionally swallowed (and `err` isn’t logged), reducing observability and making notification failures hard to detect, even though the core mutation (persisting guests) succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw `guests` passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests` (addGuests.handler.ts:170) — `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in email-manager.ts misclassifies existing attendees whose emails were re-submitted, sending them a full "scheduled" email instead of the intended "guests added" notice

`evt` (CalendarEvent) never sets the `team` field, so the team-member notification loop in `sendAddGuestsEmails` gated on `calendarEvent.team?.members` is dead code — team members are never notified when guests are added to team bookings, and `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail`'s subject silently falls back to the organizer's name instead of the team name

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the constructed `evt: CalendarEvent` includes `organizer`, `attendees`, `uid`, `location`, etc., but never sets a `team` field (nor does it fetch/include team members). In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (`packages/emails/email-manager.ts`), team notifications are only sent inside `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { ... }`, so based on the diff alone that loop will not run and team members won’t be emailed for team bookings. The second clause about `OrganizerAddGuestsEmail` subject falling back to organizer/team name isn’t supported by the shown organizer email template (it uses `this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`), but the dead team-member notification path is a verifiable behavior issue from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New guests receive the generic `AttendeeScheduledEmail` rather than a dedicated template — if that template renders cancel/reschedule booking-management links keyed to `calEvent.uid`, arbitrarily-added guests receive control links over the organizer's booking

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to emails in `newGuests` (packages/emails/email-manager.ts), while other attendees get the dedicated `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. However, the finding’s core claim—that `AttendeeScheduledEmail` renders cancel/reschedule/booking-management links keyed only to `calEvent.uid` and would therefore grant added guests control—cannot be verified from this diff because the `AttendeeScheduledEmail` template implementation and its link/auth model are not shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `&&` used instead of `||` in the `isTeamAdminOrOwner` check (addGuests.handler.ts:46-48), requiring the user to be both team admin and team owner — effectively owner-only — so team admins get FORBIDDEN in normal usage
matched_golden_ids: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same permission logic bug: using && instead of || in the admin/owner check, which incorrectly requires both roles and blocks admins.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Two sequential membership round trips (isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner each awaited separately) where one query or Promise.all would do, and both run even for non-team bookings (teamId ?? 0)

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`, which performs two sequential awaited calls (could be parallelized via `Promise.all` or combined) and also executes both membership checks even when `booking.eventType?.teamId` is null/undefined (falling back to `0`). This is a concrete, diff-grounded efficiency/logic concern, but the diff alone doesn’t prove it causes incorrect behavior or failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded `guests` array in addGuests.schema.ts (z.array with no .max()) allows a single crafted request to create thousands of attendee rows, thousands of concurrent emails, and MBs of O((a+m)²) ICS rendering, all awaited inside the mutation — a resource-exhaustion/SMTP-abuse vector with no cap and no rate limit

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `addGuests` with input schema `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` with no `.max()` (and the UI-side zod array in `AddGuestsDialog` also has no cap). In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler `createMany` inserts one attendee row per email, then builds `attendeesList` and calls `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and then `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` which constructs an `emailsToSend` array proportional to attendees/team members and `await Promise.all(emailsToSend)`. With a very large `guests` array, a single request can drive mass DB writes and mass concurrent email/ICS generation, which is a verifiable resource-exhaustion/abuse risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No check against seatsPerTimeSlot for seated events, so guest additions can exceed available seats

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` unconditionally appends new attendees via `prisma.booking.update({ data: { attendees: { createMany: ... }}})` after only filtering duplicates/blacklist, and never checks `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (which is included on the constructed `CalendarEvent` as `seatsPerTimeSlot`). For event types using seat limits, this allows adding guests beyond available seats because no capacity validation exists in the added code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server accepts duplicate emails within the input: the schema lacks the uniqueness refine the client applies, and uniqueGuests only filters against existing attendees and the blacklist without deduping within the input, so guests: ["a@x.com","a@x.com"] creates two identical attendee rows with duplicate calendar invites and emails
matched_golden_ids: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same issue: uniqueGuests only filters against existing attendees and blacklist but does not deduplicate duplicates within the submitted input, allowing createMany to insert multiple identical attendee rows when repeated emails are provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email comparisons are case-sensitive (guest === attendee.email), so case variants of the same email slip through the dedup check

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, deduplication is done with a strict case-sensitive comparison: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)`. Since neither side is normalized (e.g., `.toLowerCase()`), adding `Test@x.com` when `test@x.com` already exists will pass the filter and be treated as a new guest. The client-side uniqueness check in `AddGuestsDialog` similarly uses `new Set(emails)` without case normalization, so case variants can slip through end-to-end.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist is lowercased at line 71 but compared against the raw guest email at line 77, so Bad@Example.com bypasses the blacklist

EventManager is built from the requesting user's credentials (getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)) instead of the booking organizer's, so when the caller is an attendee or team admin there are no matching credentials and updateCalendarAttendees likely no-ops silently

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation allows non-organizers to call it (`isAttendee` or team admin/owner pass the permission check). But the calendar update is performed via `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials })`, where `user` is the *requesting* user, not `booking.user` (the organizer). This means when an attendee or other authorized non-organizer triggers `addGuests`, `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` will run using the caller’s credentials rather than the organizer’s, which is very likely incorrect for updating the organizer’s calendar event referenced by `booking`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Redundant organizer query: the booking query already includes `user` with all scalar fields, so the extra findFirstOrThrow for name/email/timeZone/locale is a wasted DB round trip on every request

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the initial `prisma.booking.findFirst({ include: { user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true }}}})` already loads the related `user` record (Prisma `include` returns all scalar fields by default). The subsequent `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 }, select: { name, email, timeZone, locale } })` is therefore an extra DB round trip that could be avoided by using `booking.user` for those fields (while keeping the include if `destinationCalendar/credentials` are needed). This is a concrete perf/efficiency issue, not a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unused eager load of the `credentials` relation for the booking's organizer (addGuests.handler.ts:38) fetches large encrypted credential payloads that are never read

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the booking is fetched with `include: { user: { include: { destinationCalendar: true, credentials: true }}}`, but the handler never reads `booking.user.credentials`. Instead it later calls `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` to obtain credentials, and only uses booking.user for destinationCalendar fallback. This makes the eager load of `credentials` unnecessary and potentially expensive (large encrypted blobs), but it’s a performance/efficiency concern rather than a functional defect.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the code builds `attendeesListPromises` by mapping over `bookingAttendees.attendees` and calling `await getTranslation(attendee.locale ?? "en", "common")` for each attendee. This is a per-attendee translation load in the request path and will scale linearly with attendee/guest count (potentially repeating the same locale). It’s a performance/efficiency concern introduced by the new handler, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email classification uses the raw `guests` input instead of `uniqueGuests`, so an existing attendee whose email was in the input (filtered out of the DB write) receives the full AttendeeScheduledEmail ("you're booked") instead of the "guests added" notice

Authorization in addGuests.handler.ts uses `&&` where `||` is intended: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` ANDs `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner`, collapsing the check to owner-only so team admins are wrongly rejected with FORBIDDEN on the new public endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. The subsequent permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` will therefore reject team admins who are not owners, likely contrary to the variable name and typical intent (admin OR owner). The finding’s “public endpoint” wording is off (the router uses `authedProcedure`), but the AND/OR authorization logic issue is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar sync runs with the requester's (session user's) credentials instead of the organizer's: `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` and `new EventManager({ ...user })` build the EventManager from the session user, so for non-organizer callers `updateCalendarAttendees` runs with the wrong (likely empty) credential set and guests are never added to the actual Google/Outlook event; the queried `booking.user.credentials` is never read.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, calendar sync is performed with the session user’s credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. The handler explicitly allows non-organizer callers (`isAttendee` or team admin/owner) to add guests, so in those cases the EventManager will likely have the wrong/empty credential set and won’t update the organizer’s external calendar event. This is reinforced by the fact that the booking query includes `user: { include: { credentials: true } }` but `booking.user.credentials` is never used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server input schema lacks the uniqueness guarantee the client enforces: the tRPC schema is just `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness refine, and the handler filters guests against existing attendees but never against each other, so `guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` passes validation and `createMany` creates duplicate Attendee rows, causing duplicate confirmation emails and duplicate calendar attendees.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`, the server accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails, but does not dedupe the input array against itself, so `guests: ["a@x.com", "a@x.com"]` remains duplicated and is passed to `attendees.createMany`. Nothing in the diff shows a DB uniqueness constraint that would prevent duplicate attendee rows, and the downstream email sending (`sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`) uses the original (possibly duplicated) input, making duplicate notifications/calendar attendee updates plausible.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The guests array is unbounded (no `.max()` constraint), so a single authenticated call can fan out thousands of outbound emails.

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC mutation input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` defines `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` (packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts). The handler then fans out emails based on attendees via `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (addGuests.handler.ts), where `sendAddGuestsEmails` builds a `Promise.all` over `calendarEvent.attendees.map(...)` plus organizer/team emails (packages/emails/email-manager.ts). Since the UI (`MultiEmail`) also allows adding an arbitrary number of email fields, a single authenticated call can submit a very large array and trigger a large number of outbound emails and DB inserts (`createMany`), which is a real abuse/DoS/spam risk exposed by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When all submitted guests already exist, the endpoint returns `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, misdescribing the condition since the submitted emails were valid and unique.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already present in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails. If all submitted guests are already attendees, `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and the handler throws `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, even though the submitted emails may be valid/unique but simply already added. This is a real, diff-grounded issue, but it’s primarily an incorrect/misleading error message rather than broken functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive email comparisons defeat the blacklist and dedup: blacklist entries are lowercased but compared against the raw guest string (so `BLOCKED@Example.com` bypasses `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`), and the `guest === attendee.email` and `isAttendee` checks are case-sensitive, allowing the same person to be added twice under different casing; emails should be normalized (trim/lowercase) at the schema boundary.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is normalized to lowercase, but the comparison uses the raw `guest` string (`!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`), so different casing can bypass the blacklist. Likewise, dedup/identity checks are case-sensitive (`guest === attendee.email` in the `uniqueGuests` filter, and `attendee.email === user.email` for `isAttendee`), allowing the same email to be treated as distinct when casing differs. The schema (`z.string().email()`) does not normalize casing/whitespace, so normalization at the boundary is not enforced.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No guard for seated event types: the handler reads `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` but never rejects seat-based bookings, and the menu entry is added unconditionally — adding plain Attendee rows to a seated booking bypasses seat accounting, ignores capacity limits, and can corrupt seat-based counts/rendering.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the code always adds new `attendees` rows via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` with no check against `booking.eventType?.seatsPerTimeSlot` (or any other capacity/seat constraints). The UI also adds the "additional_guests" menu action unconditionally in `BookingListItem.tsx`, so this mutation is exposed for any booking type. From the diff alone, this means a seat-limited (group/seated) event can have arbitrary extra attendees added, potentially exceeding the intended seat limit and breaking seat-based assumptions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Raw `guests` is passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of `uniqueGuests`, so an existing attendee whose email was re-submitted receives a full "you're booked" confirmation email instead of the guests-added notice.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server computes `uniqueGuests` by filtering out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, and only inserts `uniqueGuests` into the DB. However it calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input array (`guests`), not `uniqueGuests`. In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts), the logic `if (newGuests.includes(attendee.email)) return AttendeeScheduledEmail(...) else AttendeeAddGuestsEmail(...)` means any attendee whose email appears in the passed list will receive the full scheduled/confirmation email. Therefore, if the user submits a mix of new + already-existing attendee emails, the existing attendee email (present in `guests` but not actually newly added) will incorrectly get the scheduled email instead of the guests-added notice.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic mutation with misleading retry semantics: Attendee rows are committed before the calendar update and emails with no transaction; if `updateCalendarAttendees` throws (e.g., expired calendar credential), the caller gets an error while the guests are already persisted, and a retry hits the `uniqueGuests.length === 0` branch and fails with `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, misdescribing the real state.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the handler persists new attendees via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` before calling `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` and only wraps *email sending* in a try/catch. Since `updateCalendarAttendees` is not in a transaction and not caught, if it throws (e.g., calendar credential failure), the mutation will error while the DB already contains the added guests. On a retry with the same `guests`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and can become empty, triggering `BAD_REQUEST` with message `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, which misrepresents the state (guests were already added). This is directly implied by the ordering and logic in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failure is swallowed and the error object discarded: `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` never logs `err`, making guest-notification failures silent and undiagnosable in production.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the `sendAddGuestsEmails` call is wrapped in `try { ... } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which discards the caught `err` and only logs a generic string. This reduces observability/diagnosability of email-notification failures (no stack/message), but it doesn't directly break core functionality since the handler continues and returns success regardless.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New attendees are created with `name: ""`, so the email they receive is addressed with an empty name, greets "Hi ,", and the ICS attendee carries `CN=""`.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new attendees are persisted with `name: ""` (see `guestsFullDetails`). That same `attendee.name` is later used when building the email payload (e.g. `packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` sets `to: `${this.attendee.name} <${this.attendee.email}>``), so newly added guests will receive emails with an empty display name (and any downstream greeting/ICS CN that relies on `name` will also be empty).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `booking.userId || 0` can throw a raw Prisma error: `Booking.userId` is nullable, so if a userless booking is acted on by an authorized attendee, `findFirstOrThrow({ id: 0 })` throws Prisma's `NotFoundError` (not a `TRPCError`), returning an unlocalized 500 instead of a proper error.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer is loaded via `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. Since `booking.userId` is treated as possibly nullable (hence the `|| 0`), a booking with `userId = null` will cause the query to look for `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw Prisma's not-found error (not a `TRPCError`). This error is not caught (only email sending is in a try/catch), so the mutation can return an unhandled 500 instead of a localized `TRPCError`, matching the finding's described failure mode.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dialog state is not reset on non-cancel close: `multiEmailValue`/`isInvalidEmail` in AddGuestsDialog are reset only in the Cancel handler, so closing via the Dialog's own `onOpenChange` (X / ESC / backdrop) leaves previously typed emails and a stale validation banner in place for the next open.

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, internal state (`multiEmailValue`, `isInvalidEmail`) is only cleared in the Cancel button handler and partially in `onSuccess` (it resets `multiEmailValue` but not `isInvalidEmail`). The dialog is controlled by `<Dialog open={isOpenDialog} onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}>`, so closing via X/ESC/backdrop will call `setIsOpenDialog(false)` without resetting either state. Since the component remains mounted (rendered unconditionally in `BookingListItem`), reopening can show previously entered emails and a stale validation error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization in addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 uses `&&` instead of `||` to combine isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner, so a pure team admin (and depending on implementation a pure owner) evaluates to false and gets FORBIDDEN on team bookings they administer

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass the team-based authorization check. This will reject users who are only admins (and potentially only owners, depending on how those helpers are implemented) and lead to an incorrect `FORBIDDEN` for legitimate team administrators adding guests to team bookings.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EventManager is built with the requesting user's (ctx.user) credentials instead of the booking organizer's — should be getUsersCredentials(booking.user) — so for non-organizer callers the organizer's calendar credential is missing and updateCalendarAttendees no-ops or throws, leaving guests persisted in the DB but never added to the actual calendar event

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the calendar update is performed via `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` where `user` is `ctx.user` (the caller) and `credentials` come from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. The handler explicitly allows non-organizers (team admin/owner or even an attendee) to call this mutation, so in those cases the organizer’s calendar credentials are not used. Since the DB is updated first (`prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`) and only afterwards `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` is called, a failure/no-op in calendar syncing would leave guests persisted in DB but not reflected on the organizer’s calendar event.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic sequence: attendees are committed via createMany before the calendar sync and email sends; if a later step throws, guests are persisted but unsynced and un-emailed, and retrying with the same emails filters them all out and throws a misleading BAD_REQUEST 'emails_must_be_unique_valid' with no remove-guest flow to recover — no transaction or compensation wraps the DB write

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the DB update is committed first (`prisma.booking.update` with `attendees.createMany`), and only afterwards it performs `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and then attempts email sending. There is no transaction/rollback around these steps, and only the email step is wrapped in a `try/catch` (calendar sync is not). So if calendar sync throws (or other later logic throws), guests remain persisted but not synced/emailed. On retry, `uniqueGuests` is computed by filtering against existing `booking.attendees`, so the same emails will result in `uniqueGuests.length === 0` and throw `BAD_REQUEST` with `emails_must_be_unique_valid`, matching the finding’s recovery/UX issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failure is swallowed with zero diagnostics: the caught `err` is discarded (only a console.log with no error detail or logger) and the mutation still returns success, making a total email-notification failure indistinguishable from success and undiagnosable in production

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and then the handler still returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. The caught `err` is not logged or rethrown, so a complete notification failure is silent (no error details) and indistinguishable from success from the mutation response perspective.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema (addGuests.schema.ts) is just z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness check, unlike the client schema which refines for uniqueness, so a direct API call can insert duplicate emails in one request

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema in `addGuests.schema.ts` allows `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint, while the client dialog applies a uniqueness `refine`. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out emails already in `booking.attendees` and blacklisted emails, but it does not de-duplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array. As a result, a direct API call can submit `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` and both pass the filter (since neither is yet an attendee) and be inserted via `createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The existing-attendee comparison `guest === attendee.email` is case-sensitive, so Guest@X.com bypasses the filter and creates a duplicate attendee row

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` is computed with `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` (case-sensitive) and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where the blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not. Since `guests` comes from `z.string().email()` without normalization, an input like `Guest@x.com` can bypass the existing-attendee check (and potentially the blacklist) if the stored email is `guest@x.com`, leading to duplicate attendee rows being created via `attendees.createMany`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The blacklist is lowercased (lines 70-72) but compared against the raw guest email (line 77), so EVIL@x.com bypasses the blacklisted evil@x.com, defeating the abuse control entirely

The check-then-createMany pattern is a TOCTOU race: concurrent requests can both pass the filter, yielding duplicate rows if there is no unique constraint on (bookingId, email) or an unhandled raw Prisma P2002 500 if there is

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, new guests are first filtered against the currently loaded `booking.attendees` (`uniqueGuests = guests.filter(!booking.attendees.some(...))`) and then inserted via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)`. This check-then-insert is non-atomic: concurrent requests can both see the same pre-state and both attempt to insert the same `(bookingId, email)` attendee. The diff shows no `skipDuplicates`, no transaction/locking, and no handling for a potential Prisma unique violation (e.g., P2002) around the `update/createMany`, so this can yield duplicate rows (if no DB constraint) or an unhandled error (if a unique constraint exists).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded guests array: no .max() on the schema and no per-request/per-user limit, so any permitted caller — including a mere external attendee — can submit thousands of emails, triggering thousands of synchronous sendEmail calls plus a calendar attendee update inside a single HTTP mutation (latency, mail-server reputation damage, cost abuse)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `addGuests` mutation whose input schema `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()` or other limit (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`). The handler allows any attendee to call it (`isAttendee` check in `addGuests.handler.ts`) and then (1) performs a calendar update (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`) and (2) sends emails to organizer/team members and all attendees/guests via `sendAddGuestsEmails`, which maps over `calendarEvent.attendees` and enqueues `sendEmail` calls and awaits `Promise.all` (`packages/emails/email-manager.ts`). With an unbounded guests array, a permitted caller can trigger very large DB writes (`createMany`), large calendar updates, and mass email sending in a single request, constituting a real abuse/DoS/cost risk introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findFirstOrThrow({ id: booking.userId || 0 }) leaks a raw Prisma P2025 error (not a TRPCError) when booking.userId is null, giving the client an opaque INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a handled response

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is null/undefined, this queries `id: 0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw a Prisma "record not found" (P2025-like) error, which is not converted to a `TRPCError` anywhere in this handler. That would surface to the client as an unhandled/internal error instead of a deliberate TRPC response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: evt.team is never populated in the CalendarEvent built by the handler, so the team-member notification loop in email-manager.ts (calendarEvent.team?.members) is dead code and team members silently receive no notification for team/round-robin bookings

adjudication.rationale: In addGuests.handler.ts the CalendarEvent `evt` is constructed without any `team` field (only organizer, attendees, uid, etc.). Yet sendAddGuestsEmails() in email-manager.ts checks `calendarEvent.team?.members` to notify team members. From the diff, nothing populates `evt.team` or includes team/member data when loading the booking (`include: { eventType: true }` but not `eventType: { include: { team: { include: { members: ... }}}}`). As written, the team-member notification loop will never run for this handler’s event object, so team members won’t receive the add-guests email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AddGuestsDialog state is not reset when closed via onOpenChange (only the Cancel button resets multiEmailValue/isInvalidEmail), so reopening shows a stale 'Emails must be unique and valid' error banner plus leftover emails from the previous session

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, the dialog’s open state is controlled by `<Dialog open={isOpenDialog} onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}>`, but local state (`multiEmailValue`, `isInvalidEmail`) is only reset in the Cancel button handler and on mutation success. If the user closes the dialog via `onOpenChange` (e.g., clicking outside/ESC), `setIsOpenDialog(false)` runs without clearing those states, so reopening can show the prior emails and a stale `emails_must_be_unique_valid` error banner (`isInvalidEmail` remains true).

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking-status guard: guests can be added to CANCELLED/REJECTED bookings, which emails all attendees an ICS with method REQUEST and status CONFIRMED that mail clients can use to resurrect the cancelled event in attendee calendars

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` updates attendees and sends calendar/email updates for any booking ID it can load, without checking any booking status/state (e.g., cancelled/rejected) before calling `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)`. The new email templates generate an ICS with `method: "REQUEST"` and `status: "CONFIRMED"` (`attendee-add-guests-email.ts`, `organizer-add-guests-email.ts`), so if this mutation is invoked on a cancelled/rejected booking, it would emit a confirmed REQUEST update that could re-add/re-confirm the event in clients. The absence of a booking-status guard is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: sendAddGuestsEmails receives the raw guests input instead of the actually-added uniqueGuests, so an existing attendee whose email was re-submitted (and filtered out of the DB insert) is classified as new and receives a full re-confirmation email instead of the guests-added notice
matched_golden_ids: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same bug: sendAddGuestsEmails determines email type for each existing attendee by checking membership in the input guests list (raw/newGuests) rather than the actually-added/unique guests. This can misclassify re-submitted existing attendees as “new” and send the wrong email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No timeout around the external calendar call and email fan-out inside the mutation, so a hung provider stalls the HTTP request until client-side timeouts

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the mutation awaits `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and then awaits `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` (which does a `Promise.all` fan-out) with no timeout/circuit-breaker/wrapping (e.g. `Promise.race`). Because these are awaited inside the request lifecycle, a slow or hung external calendar provider call (inside `updateCalendarAttendees`) or an email send that never resolves could keep the mutation from returning. This is a reliability/latency concern introduced by the new feature, but not a strictly verifiable functional defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Authorization logic in addGuests.handler.ts uses `&&` where `||` is intended: the `isTeamAdminOrOwner` check requires the user to be both team admin AND team owner, silently denying permission to team admins who are not owners and breaking the feature for an entire user class

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed with `&&`: `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0))`. This requires a user to be both a team admin and a team owner to pass the permission check. Given the variable name and typical authorization semantics, team admins who are not owners will be denied (`FORBIDDEN`) even though they likely should be allowed, breaking the feature for that user class.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Uniqueness validation is enforced only on the client: AddGuestsDialog re-declares its own ZAddGuestsInputSchema (different shape, re-instantiated every render) with a uniqueness refine that the server schema lacks, and the handler's uniqueGuests filter only checks existing attendees — a direct tRPC call with duplicate emails passes server validation and reaches createMany with duplicate rows, inserting duplicates or throwing a raw Prisma error

adjudication.rationale: The client dialog enforces uniqueness via a locally-defined `ZAddGuestsInputSchema = z.array(...).refine(...)` inside `AddGuestsDialog`, but the server tRPC input schema (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts`) only validates `{ bookingId, guests: z.array(z.string().email()) }` with no uniqueness constraint. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate the incoming `guests` array, so a direct tRPC call with duplicated emails can produce duplicated entries in `guestsFullDetails` and be passed to `attendees.createMany`, which can insert duplicates or trigger a Prisma constraint error depending on DB constraints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No email normalization: the lowercased blacklist is compared against un-normalized guest emails so `User@Spam.com` bypasses a `user@spam.com` blacklist entry, and case-sensitive comparisons (`guest === attendee.email`, `isAttendee` check, `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)`) allow duplicate attendees with case-mismatched emails and deny legitimate attendees with case-mismatched session emails

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but the filter checks `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` without normalizing `guest`, so case-variants can bypass the blacklist. The code also performs multiple case-sensitive email comparisons (`guest === attendee.email` when filtering duplicates, `attendee.email === user.email` for `isAttendee`, and `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` in `sendAddGuestsEmails`), which can allow duplicate attendees differing only by case and can incorrectly deny access for legitimate attendees whose session email casing differs from stored attendee casing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Handler passes the raw input `guests` to sendAddGuestsEmails instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`, so an email that was already an attendee (filtered out server-side, no row created) receives a full AttendeeScheduledEmail ('you're booked') instead of the guests-added notification

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the server filters `guests` into `uniqueGuests` (excluding already-existing attendees and blacklisted emails) and only creates attendee rows for `uniqueGuests`, but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the raw input. In `email-manager.ts`, `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide to send `AttendeeScheduledEmail` vs `AttendeeAddGuestsEmail`. If the caller included an email that was already an attendee (filtered out, no new row), that attendee is still in `evt.attendees` and will match `guests.includes(...)`, causing them to incorrectly receive the full scheduled email instead of the guests-added notification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email sending failures are swallowed: the catch block discards the caught `err`, logs a static string via `console.log` instead of the codebase logger, and the mutation returns success — notification failures become completely unobservable with no error object, log level, or monitoring signal

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, email sending is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` and the handler then returns `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This does swallow the caught `err` (not logged/propagated), uses `console.log` with a static string (no error object/level/structured logger), and makes email notification failures hard to observe while still reporting success for the mutation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent error handling for side effects after the DB commit: `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` runs unguarded while the adjacent email call is wrapped in a swallow-everything catch; if the calendar update throws, the mutation rejects even though guests were persisted, and the user's retry hits the confusing `emails_must_be_unique_valid` BAD_REQUEST

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, guests are persisted via `prisma.booking.update(... attendees.createMany ...)` before calling side effects. The calendar side effect `await eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking);` is not guarded, so if it throws, the mutation rejects even though DB changes already committed. A subsequent retry will compute `uniqueGuests` as empty because the emails now exist in `booking.attendees`, triggering `throw new TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, matching the finding. Meanwhile, the adjacent email side effect is wrapped in a broad try/catch that swallows errors, creating inconsistent post-commit behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MultiEmailLazy is a copy-pasted lazy wrapper with a false justification comment: the '40kb' claim is lifted from PhoneInputLazy, but MultiEmail is a small form component — the lazy wrapper is premature optimization, the comment is actively misleading, and the `as unknown as typeof import(...)` double cast came along for the ride

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `packages/ui/form/MultiEmailLazy.tsx` with a copy-pasted comment `/** These are like 40kb that not every user needs */` and a `dynamic(() => import("./MultiEmail")) as unknown as typeof import("./MultiEmail").default;` double-cast. In the same diff, `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` is introduced and is a small, simple form component (~<100 LOC) with no obvious heavy dependencies shown, so the blanket “40kb” justification looks misleading/unsubstantiated in this context, and the wrapper adds complexity (type casting + dynamic import) without clear need evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded English string 'Remove email' in MultiEmail's Tooltip bypasses `t()` while the same component uses `t("add_another")` two lines away, shipping untranslated in all non-English locales

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the Tooltip uses a hardcoded string `content="Remove email"` while the same component otherwise uses i18n via `const { t } = useLocale()` and `t("add_another")`. This will display English text in non-English locales, an i18n inconsistency introduced by the diff, but it doesn't break functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead fallback in the error toast: the template literal `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}` is always truthy, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never take the fallback, making the `unable_to_add_guests` locale key unreachable dead code

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog.tsx` the `onError` handler builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}`;` and then calls `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")`. A template literal always returns a string, so `message` will be truthy even when `err.data?.code` is `undefined` (e.g. it becomes `"undefined: ..."`). Therefore the `unable_to_add_guests` fallback is unreachable and users may see an unhelpful `undefined:` prefix instead of the intended generic error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent 'members' naming for a guests feature: the menu id `add_members` and testid `add_members` say 'members' while the feature, label, locale keys, and mutation all say 'guests', so future greps for 'guests' will miss these and e2e tests will encode the wrong domain term

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces a guests feature (e.g., `AddGuestsDialog`, `trpc.viewer.bookings.addGuests`, locale keys like `additional_guests`, `guests_added`), but the action/menu item uses `id: "add_members"` in `BookingListItem.tsx` and the dialog submit button uses `data-testid="add_members"` in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`. adjudication_records.issue_text: Unused flexibility in MultiEmail: `readOnly` and `placeholder` props are dead paths — the only caller passes `readOnly={false}` and no placeholder, making the entire readOnly branch and placeholder plumbing speculative YAGNI complexity in a component with exactly one consumer

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `MultiEmail` introducing `readOnly` and `placeholder` props and a single new caller (`AddGuestsDialog`) passing `readOnly={false}` and no `placeholder`. While it’s true that this caller doesn’t exercise the read-only branch, the props are still implemented and could be used by other consumers (the component is exported from `packages/ui/index.tsx`). Calling this “dead paths” / “YAGNI complexity” is a subjective style/abstraction critique rather than a concrete, diff-verifiable problem.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated 'add email' button blocks in MultiEmail (lines 56-76 and 83-96) differ only in label/testid while both perform the same array-push-and-setValue logic; they will drift (one already has `variant="button"` and different margins the other lacks) and should be extracted into one handler/button

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx` there are two separate `<Button>` blocks that both create `updatedValue = [...value]; updatedValue.push(""); setValue(updatedValue);`: the "add another" button inside the `value.length ? ...` branch (around lines 56-76 in the new file) and the initial "add emails" button rendered when `!value.length && !readOnly` (around lines 83-96). adjudication_records.issue_text: Team permission check in addGuests.handler.ts:46-48 uses && instead of ||, requiring the user to be both team admin AND owner, so a team admin who isn't an owner gets FORBIDDEN on a booking they should manage

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`, which requires the user to be both a team admin and a team owner. This contradicts the variable name and likely intended permission logic (admin OR owner). As written, a team admin who is not also an owner will fail the permission gate `if (!isTeamAdminOrOwner && !isOrganizer && !isAttendee)` and receive `FORBIDDEN` even though team admins typically should be authorized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blacklist guard is case-bypassable: env list is lowercased but guest emails are compared raw, so Bad@Example.com bypasses a blacklist entry of bad@example.com

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bypass: the blacklist entries are lowercased but the incoming guest email is not normalized before includes() comparison, so uppercase variants can evade BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server schema (addGuests.schema.ts) omits the uniqueness validation the client enforces, so a direct mutation with duplicate emails creates duplicate Attendee rows that propagate to the calendar event and trigger duplicate emails

adjudication.rationale: The server-side input schema `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.schema.ts` only validates `guests` as `z.array(z.string().email())` and does not enforce uniqueness like the client’s `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` refine in `AddGuestsDialog.tsx`. In `addGuests.handler.ts`, `uniqueGuests` filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the incoming `guests` array, so duplicate emails in the mutation input can remain and be passed to `attendees.createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendee rows. Those duplicates then flow into `attendeesList` and `sendAddGuestsEmails`, which maps over `calendarEvent.attendees` and would send duplicate emails for duplicated attendee entries.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials via getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) instead of the organizer's credentials, causing updateCalendarAttendees to silently no-op when a team admin or attendee invokes the endpoint

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the endpoint permits non-organizers to invoke it (`isTeamAdminOrOwner` or `isAttendee`), but the calendar update is performed using the caller’s credentials: `const credentials = await getUsersCredentials(ctx.user);` and `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })`, then `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`. The organizer is fetched separately (`organizer = await prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow(...)`) but their credentials are never used for the calendar update, so when a team admin/attendee calls this mutation it may be unable to update the organizer’s connected calendar even though it updates DB attendees.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Partial-failure cascade: DB write commits before calendar/emails, so if the calendar update throws, guests are already persisted with no emails sent, and retrying yields a nonsense BAD_REQUEST: emails_must_be_unique_valid error with no way to re-trigger emails

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler` the DB update (`prisma.booking.update` creating attendees) happens before the external side effects (`eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` and `sendAddGuestsEmails`). There is no transaction/compensation, and `updateCalendarAttendees` is not wrapped in a try/catch, so if it throws the guests are already persisted but calendar/emails won’t run. On retry, `uniqueGuests` filters out already-persisted attendees and can become empty, triggering `TRPCError({ code: "BAD_REQUEST", message: "emails_must_be_unique_valid" })`, preventing re-triggering of calendar/email updates. This matches the partial-failure cascade described.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unbounded guest list with no cap on array length plus any-attendee permission check allows any authed attendee to mass-email thousands of addresses through the platform mailer with no rate limit

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC mutation `addGuests` accepts `guests: z.array(z.string().email())` with no `.max()`/length cap (`addGuests.schema.ts`), and the UI (`MultiEmail`) allows pushing arbitrary additional entries. On the server, `addGuestsHandler` permits any authenticated attendee of the booking (`isAttendee`) to call it, then `createMany` inserts all provided emails and `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` triggers email sends across `calendarEvent.attendees` (i.e., scales with the number of added guests). No throttling/rate limiting or size guard is shown in this diff, so an attendee can submit a very large list and cause mass outbound email.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Email failures are swallowed with catch (err) { console.log(...) } — the error object is never logged and console.log instead of the logger means production monitoring sees nothing

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests); } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }`, which swallows the exception, does not log `err`, and uses `console.log` rather than an application logger. This is a concrete observability/monitoring issue introduced by the diff, though not necessarily a functional defect since the handler intentionally continues after email failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Team-member email loop in sendAddGuestsEmails is dead code because the evt literal built in the handler never sets team, so team members silently get no notifications

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the `evt: CalendarEvent` literal passed to `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` does not set any `team` field (it only sets `organizer`, `attendees`, etc.). In `sendAddGuestsEmails` (`packages/emails/email-manager.ts`), the team-member notification loop is guarded by `if (calendarEvent.team?.members) { ... }`, so unless `formatCalEvent(calEvent)` can somehow synthesize `team` from the provided `calEvent` (not shown in the diff), that branch will never run and team members won’t receive notifications. This matches the finding: the loop is effectively dead given the event object constructed in the handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Case-sensitive email matching throughout (guest === attendee.email and attendee.email === user.email) creates duplicate rows for the same person with different casing and denies legitimate attendees with FORBIDDEN

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, guest de-duplication and permission checks compare emails with strict, case-sensitive equality: `guest === attendee.email` when filtering `uniqueGuests`, and `attendee.email === user.email` for `isAttendee`. Since emails are not normalized (e.g., lowercased) anywhere in the shown code, the same mailbox with different casing can bypass the duplicate check (creating multiple attendee rows differing only by case) and can cause a legitimate attendee to fail `isAttendee` and hit the `FORBIDDEN` path. This is a correctness/authorization defect grounded directly in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No booking-status check in the handler, so adding guests to a cancelled booking sends ICS invites hardcoded to status CONFIRMED for a non-existent event and attempts a calendar update against a likely-deleted event

adjudication.rationale: The new `addGuestsHandler` fetches the booking and proceeds to update attendees, call `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)`, and send ICS emails without any guard on booking state (no check like `booking.status` / `booking.cancelledAt` etc. appears in the diff). Separately, the new email templates hardcode ICS `status: "CONFIRMED"` in both `packages/emails/templates/attendee-add-guests-email.ts` and `packages/emails/templates/organizer-add-guests-email.ts`. While the finding’s claim about a "likely-deleted event" isn’t verifiable from the diff, the absence of a booking-status gate combined with always-CONFIRMED ICS is a concrete edge-case concern introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Success is reported even when some requested guests were silently dropped (blacklisted or duplicates), returning 'Guests added' without indicating what was dropped, so the user believes all addresses were added

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuestsHandler`, the server filters the requested `guests` into `uniqueGuests` by dropping emails that are already attendees or are in `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` (see `uniqueGuests = guests.filter(...)`). If at least one remains, it proceeds, updates the booking with only `uniqueGuests`, and always returns `{ message: "Guests added" }` with no information about which inputs were skipped. The client `AddGuestsDialog` then unconditionally shows `showToast(t("guests_added"), "success")` on mutation success. This matches the finding: partial success is reported as full success, and dropped addresses are silent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: booking.userId || 0 with findFirstOrThrow causes an unhandled Prisma P2025 500 error for bookings with null userId, and the dialog's onError interpolates err.data?.code producing garbage like 'undefined: No User found...'

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, organizer lookup uses `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is null/undefined (suggested by the `|| 0`), this will query `id=0` and `findFirstOrThrow` will throw (commonly Prisma P2025). There is no surrounding error handling, so the mutation can fail with an unhandled server error. Separately, the dialog’s `onError` builds `const message = `${err.data?.code}: ${t(err.message)}``, which will render a garbage prefix like `undefined:` when `err.data?.code` is absent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dialog state is only reset via the Cancel button — closing via ESC/backdrop (onOpenChange) doesn't reset multiEmailValue or isInvalidEmail, and isInvalidEmail is never cleared on the success path, leaving stale emails and a stale error banner

adjudication.rationale: In `AddGuestsDialog`, the `Dialog` uses `onOpenChange={setIsOpenDialog}`, so closing via ESC/backdrop will only flip `isOpenDialog` without resetting local state. `multiEmailValue` and `isInvalidEmail` are only reset in the Cancel button handler, and on success only `multiEmailValue` is reset (`setMultiEmailValue([""])`) while `isInvalidEmail` is not cleared. This can leave a stale error banner (and potentially stale entered emails if closed without Cancel) when reopening the dialog.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TOCTOU race on the dedupe check: attendee-existence check reads the booking then createMany happens later with no transaction or DB-level uniqueness on (bookingId, email), so concurrent calls both insert duplicate attendees

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the code dedupes against `booking.attendees` read from an earlier `findFirst` (`uniqueGuests = guests.filter(!booking.attendees.some(...))`) and only later does a separate `prisma.booking.update({ attendees: { createMany: ... }})` with no transaction/locking. The diff does not show any DB-level unique constraint on (bookingId,email), so concurrent mutations could both pass the stale dedupe check and attempt to insert the same attendee email. Whether it becomes an actual duplicate vs. a DB constraint error can’t be verified from this diff alone, but the TOCTOU concern is grounded in the shown logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Hardcoded untranslated string 'Remove email' in MultiEmail.tsx Tooltip bypasses t() while the rest of the component is internationalized

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/ui/form/MultiEmail.tsx`, the Tooltip uses a hardcoded user-facing string `content="Remove email"` while the rest of the component uses `t()` for labels (e.g., `t("add_another")`). This bypasses localization and is an i18n inconsistency introduced by the diff, but it doesn’t break functionality.
